proposition: Using a normalised weighted sign position (each sign's position reduced to a standard text length of ten signs, with sign positions weighted linearly by the original text length), Indus signs can be classified by their preferred position as Initial, Early-Medial, Mid-Medial, Late-Medial, Terminal, constant, or constant but not initial or not terminal; doubling, mirroring, hatching, or marking a sign can change its positional classification; and signs 382, 790, 832, and 892 are good candidates for syllables, because syllables should have an almost constant positional distribution while logograms and grammatical markers should fall on restricted syntactic positions.
